scope: Distinguish the legacy DXF SOLID entity from ACIS-bearing 3DSOLID and refresh the existing Assimp DXF peer lane by family, format direction, and projection loss; refine plan readiness without implementation changes.

method.kind: Primary Autodesk DXF/ObjectARX documentation plus static read-only review of Assimp source and issue history
method.assimpSourcePin: Mutable master URL reviewed statically; immutable commit SHA was not acquired in this pass. The prior pinned-source and Assimp 6.0.5 runtime evidence in the plan remain separate.
method.evidenceBoundary: Autodesk sources define entity naming and public DXF fields. Assimp branch review is source-level observation only, with no immutable pin or runtime result. The issue report is not a reproduced defect or proof of ACIS 3DSOLID behavior. No support claim is promoted.

evidence.topic: SOLID and 3DSOLID are distinct DXF entity families
observed: Autodesk describes SOLID as a 2D entity and documents four corner points plus optional thickness and extrusion direction.

Autodesk documents 3DSOLID, REGION, and BODY as AcDbModelerGeometry records with proprietary group-1 data and optional group-3 continuation; the 3DSOLID table also identifies a history soft-owner handle.
The names must not be normalized to one ambiguous 'solid' category or treated as interchangeable ACIS evidence.
evidence.planUse: Keep legacy 2D SOLID compatibility distinct from modeler-carrier transport, ownership/history, B-rep validity, and native 3D acceptance. Use literal DXF entity identity in feature inventories and denominators.

evidence.topic: Assimp is a narrow ASCII explicit-geometry projection, not an ACIS or general DXF oracle
observed: The inspected current DXFLoader.cpp explicitly refuses binary DXF.
Its block/entity dispatch handles POLYLINE, root INSERT, 3DFACE, LINE/3DLINE, and POINT; no SOLID, 3DSOLID, MESH, REGION, or BODY dispatch route was observed.
The PFACE vertex path has a four-index array and ignores additional face references after warning; negative signed references are converted to absolute values, losing visibility-edge signs.

The importer projects records into layer-oriented aiMesh output rather than preserving the CAD entity/owner graph or an ACIS B-rep. Existing plan evidence separately records axis conversion, ignored INSERT rotation, and nested-INSERT block-loss behavior.
evidence.planUse: Admit only family-filtered, ASCII-only explicit-geometry observations with a per-source-entity disposition ledger. Exclude binary, nested/rotated INSERT, PFACE visibility-sign, and greater-than-four-reference PFACE cells from positive comparator coverage.

evidence.topic: Assimp issue #2645 wording is not ACIS 3DSOLID evidence
observed: Issue #2645 reports a DXF file described as using SOLID and an importer message that no 3D data was found.
The issue history shows it was closed as not planned and later reopened to join discussion; the attached drawing was not downloaded or executed in this review.
Given Autodesk's entity distinction, the report does not establish a 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY, ACIS payload, or native solid-reader failure.
evidence.planUse: Do not use the issue as a libdxfrw defect, as a 3DSOLID peer failure, or as a reason to expand the Assimp runtime matrix. Keep it as a nomenclature and comparator-eligibility warning.

nextActions: Continue the existing ready local implementation queue; no new Assimp run or installation is needed.
For any future comparison, pin an immutable Assimp source/package first, classify literal DXF names, and count every source entity as typed, projected, omitted, or rejected.
Keep SOLID/TRACE 2D compatibility separate from 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY modeler carrier and semantic gates.
